- Verdicts: repository likely to fail at 10k+ concurrent active users without fixes; failure at 100k and 1M.

findings.title: Excessive DB calls / N+1 risk in TradeDetailsPage and dashboard flows
findings.detail: Graph-identified flows TradeDetailsPage (flowId=06d73f78-5f64-4ef2-93c6-6aa19f0a22a1 and 48bb6dc1-6950-4501-846e-b0616aceb8a3) show dbCallCount=30 and hasN1Risk=true. Entry files src/app/dashboard/positions/[id]/page.tsx and src/app/dashboard/trades/[id]/page.tsx call actions/trade.ts::getAllTrades and other actions (getTradeExits, getTradePyramids, getDashboardData) producing dozens of DB calls per render.
findings.breaksAt: Approximately 10k concurrent active page loads — per-page ~30 DB calls will multiply and exhaust DB resources
findings.fix: Batch related DB requests: collect IDs and fetch related rows with a single findMany WHERE id IN (...) or use include relations. Remove per-item findMany inside loops. Apply pagination/limits. Reuse the batching pattern used in actions/dashboard.ts where appropriate.

findings.title: No caching layer for hot read paths (live prices and dashboard data)
findings.detail: getCurrentMarketPrices (actions/trade.ts lines 780–986) queries livePrice and falls back to dailyClose. getDashboardData calls getCurrentMarketPrices and multiple trade/fund queries. getDependencies shows no cache library in repo dependencies — hot reads hit DB on every page load.
findings.breaksAt: 100k+ users — heavy read traffic will cause high DB CPU/I/O and increased latency
findings.fix: Introduce a caching layer (Redis or similar) for live prices and per-profile dashboard snapshots with short TTLs. Cache dailyClose/lookups and memoize expensive aggregations. Consider edge/CDN caching for non-user-specific endpoints.

dependencies: No redis/memcached packages found in getDependencies output
notes: getCurrentMarketPrices uses livePrice.findMany and dailyClose.findMany fallback; getDashboardData calls getCurrentMarketPrices

findings.title: Prisma singleton present but explicit pool parameters not configured; relies on prisma-accelerate
findings.detail: src/lib/prisma.ts exports a global PrismaClient singleton (good) and sets transaction timeouts. getDependencies lists @prisma/extension-accelerate; checkConnectionPool detected serverless Next framework and prisma-accelerate as external pooler. However explicit pool limits/timeouts are not configured in repo and DATABASE_URL settings were not found.
findings.breaksAt: 100k–1M users if external pooler is misconfigured or removed — pool exhaustion/timeouts possible
findings.fix: Verify prisma-accelerate configuration in deployment and ensure pool limits are appropriate. Maintain the global singleton pattern. Where supported, set explicit pool and timeout parameters or ensure platform pooler has suitable limits. Add monitoring/alerts for connection exhaustion.

findings.title: Large OR arrays for market-price lookups can create expensive query plans
findings.detail: getCurrentMarketPrices constructs an OR array of {symbol,exchange,segment} and calls prisma.livePrice.findMany({ where: { OR: orConditions } }). For large symbol sets this becomes a long OR clause in SQL causing slow planning and suboptimal index usage. The fallback dailyClose.findMany uses distinct + orderBy(date desc) which is potentially expensive despite an index on [symbol,exchange,segment,date].
findings.breaksAt: 100k users when many symbols are queried per request or many concurrent dashboard loads occur
findings.fix: Use tuple IN queries (WHERE (symbol,exchange,segment) IN (...)) or batch symbol lookups server-side. Consider temporary tables/UNNEST joins for very large sets. Cache price maps to reduce DB queries.

files: actions/trade.ts (construction of orConditions and livePrice.findMany around lines 864-896)
schema: prisma/schema.prisma shows DailyClose @@index([symbol, exchange, segment, date])

findings.title: Multi-step edit flows perform multiple writes without explicit transaction boundaries
findings.detail: Flows such as handleEditSubmit (flowId=bb4daf8c-1f22-4376-b336-3c786660af1a) call updateTrade and then functions that update related funds and recalculate state (updateTradeEntryFund, recalculateTradeStatus, recalculateAverageEntryPrice). The surfaced code paths do not show these multi-write sequences wrapped in a transaction, risking partial updates under concurrent edits.
findings.breaksAt: 100k users with concurrent edits — risk of inconsistent state and race conditions
findings.fix: Wrap related writes in prisma.$transaction or equivalent to ensure atomicity, or use optimistic locking/serializable transactions. Add idempotency, retries and tests for concurrent edit scenarios.
